GetRaceEntryItemByHorsePaged.commentStewards: Rdr reported the gelding was not comfortable racing in an anticlockwise direction and was disappointing. A post-race vet exam did not reveal any significant findings. A sample was taken for analysis. Tnr rep concurred with the views of rdr that the gelding did not appear to travel comfortably in the anticlockwise direction, and added it will be assessed in the days subsequent, with consideration given to the transfer of the gelding back to the Sydney stable.

GetRaceEntryItemByHorsePaged.comment: Jumped Fast Restrained today thus Settled Down last 12 Lengths ridden quiet @ rear within 6 Lengths Straightening Up into 3rd x 300m, into 2nd x 25m - and N. Rawiller pleaded guilty to a charge under AR132(7)(a)(ii) for having used the whip on 10 occasions prior to the 100m, five more than is permitted under the rule. N. Rawiller?s licence to ride in races was suspended for a period to commence on Sunday, 19 April 2026 and to expire on Sunday, 26 April 2026, on which day he may ride. In addition, N. Rawiller was fined $7,500. In assessing penalty Stewards were mindful of N. Rawiller's poor record in relation to this rule. - # Sound eff/finale
GetRaceEntryItemByHorsePaged.commentStewards: When questioned re riding in early stages & reason for settling at rear, rdr std he intended to settle in or near lead, however after beginning satisfactorily, several inside runners showed significant early pace & he felt he would have had to make too much use of mnt to obtain lead, so after travelling 100m he elected to ease & ride it more conservatively. Added after passing the crossing near the 1700m his mnt commenced to travel strongly when positioned to the outside of a runner, so for this reason he further restrained to the rear of field where it travelled comfortably.

GetRaceEntryItemByHorsePaged.commentStewards: Rdr reported he was able to lead as anticipated, whereby his mnt travelled satisfactorily through the early and middle stages, however it came under heavy pressure soon after straightening, failed to respond to his riding and weakened, and when out of contention he did not test it fully over the final 200m. A post-race vet exam revealed the gelding to have cardiac arrhythmia. Tnr was advised of the provisions of the RA Code of Practice under AR88B(2)(b). Vet clearance since received.
